newsitem.title: USA: INSIGHT-Dlr/yen path higher guarded by 114.60/90.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT-Dlr/yen path higher guarded by 114.60/90.

text.p: Dollar/yen has tentatively carved out a short-term base around 112 but resistance between 114.60 and 114.90 is blocking a big recovery, analysts said.

The daily charts look somewhat more bullish for dollar/yen, after its swift, 12-percent fall from 127.47 yen on May 1 to 111.98 on Tuesday. But considering the scale of the decline, the dollar's retracement to 114.45 yen on Wednesday looks unimpressive, they said.
"Two-and-a-half-yen higher looks like nothing, it's still a modest correction considering where we've been," said Scott Siller, senior technical analyst at MCM CurrencyWatch.
Intermediate resistance lies around 114.60 yen but the upside risk extends to 114.90 yen, where Siller said rising resistance from a nascent rising wedge pattern is placed.
"I'm looking for upside failure between (114.65 and 114.90 yen). We protect ourselves over 115 and we'll be okay," he said.

Randolph Donney, director of capital markets research at Pegasus Econometric Group, said interday trading in dollar/yen was still choppy and consolidative, with initial minor support placed around 113.35/40 yen on Wednesday.
It looks like a tentative short-term base is forming but speculators won't get comfortable until dollar/yen closes above 114.75, Donney said.
"We may have finally plumbed some support in dollar/yen," Donney said. "To confirm that though, I think we have to get above 114.75, which was the breakdown point."
If support at 112 fails, dollar/yen could head for 109.30, the 38-percent retracement target of the entire rally from 79.75 in April 1995, to this month's high, Siller said.
Pit-stops at 111.25 and 110.60 yen could come on the way down, he said.
Meanwhile, dollar/mark experienced volatile interday trading, within a broad 1.6705 to 1.7090 range, analysts said.
While dollar/mark is also showing signs of basing, after failing to make a new low on Wednesday, the daily charts aren't as bullish as they are in dollar/yen, Donney said.
"We're making progress here if we get above 1.7005 (marks)," Donney said. "That would be another step in the right direction for bulls."
At 1200 EDT/1600 GMT on Wednesday, the dollar was trading at1.6915/25 marks, up from 1.6870/80 at the open and at 113.94/99 yen, up from 113.60/70. ((--Alden Bentley, 212 859 1667))
